p0.original: 第五章 感受的根源
p0.en: Chapter V. The roots of feeling

p1.original: 听到不中听的话：四种选择
p1.en: Hear what you don't hear: four options

p2.original: 非暴力沟通强调，感受的根源在于我们自身。我们的需要和期待，以及对他人言行的看法，导致了我们的感受。
p2.en: Nonviolent Communication emphasizes that the roots of feelings lie in ourselves. Our needs and expectations, as well as our perceptions of others ' words and deeds, have led to our feelings.

p3.original: 听到不中听的话时，我们有四种选择。
p3.en: We have four choices when we hear what is not heard.

p4.original: 第一种是认为自己犯了错。例如，有人气愤地说：“我从没见过像你这么自私的人！”这时，我们可能会自责：“哦，我没有考虑别人的感受，真是太自私了！”这会导致我们内疚、惭愧，甚至厌恶自己。
p4.en: The first is to think that you have made a mistake. For example, some are angry and say, "I've never seen a man as selfish as you!" "Oh, I didn't take into account the feelings of others. It's selfish! This can lead us to guilt, shame, and even hate ourselves.

p5.original: 第二种是指责对方。这时，我们也许会驳斥对方：“你没有权利这么说！我一直都很在乎你的感受。你才自私！”在争吵时，我们一般会感到恼怒。
p5.en: The second is to blame each other. At this point, we might rebut each other: “You have no right to say this!” I've always cared about how you felt. You're selfish! We're usually angry when we argue.

p6.original: 第三种是了解我们的感受和需要。这时，我们可能会发现我们有些伤心，因为我们看重信任和接纳。
p6.en: The third is to know what we feel and what we need. At that point, we may find ourselves somewhat sad because we value trust and acceptance.

p7.original: 第四种是用心体会他人的感受和需要。这时，我们也许就会想“他伤心可能是因为他需要体贴和支持”。
p7.en: The fourth is to feel the feelings and needs of others. At that point, we might think, “He may be sad because he needs care and support”.

p8.original: 通过了解我们的需要、愿望、期待以及想法，我们不再指责他人，而承认我们的感受源于自身。
p8.en: By understanding our needs, aspirations, expectations and ideas, we no longer blame others, but recognize that our feelings derive from ourselves.

p9.original: 请注意以下例句表达失望的方式有何不同。
p9.en: Please note the difference in the manner in which disappointment is expressed in the following examples.

p11.original: 甲：你昨晚没来令我很失望。
p11.en: A: I was disappointed you didn't come last night.

p12.original: 乙：昨晚你没来，我很失望，因为我想和你说一些烦心事。
p12.en: B: I'm disappointed you didn't show up last night because I wanted to tell you something.

p13.original: 在上面的例句中，甲认为，她的感受是由他人的行为引起的。而乙认为，她感到失望，是因为她的愿望没有得到满足。
p13.en: In the preceding sentence, A, it is argued that her feelings are caused by the behaviour of others. She was disappointed because her wishes had not been met.

p15.original: 甲：他们取消了合同让我很不高兴。
p15.en: A: I'm not happy that they cancelled the contract.

p16.original: 乙：他们取消了合同，我很不高兴，因为我对自己说这是极不负责任的行为。
p16.en: B: They cancelled the contract, and I was unhappy because I said to myself that it was a very irresponsible act.

p17.original: 在这个例子中，甲认为，他人的行为使她不高兴；而乙认识到，她的观点使她不愉快。在非暴力沟通中，我们还鼓励乙进一步了解她的愿望：她的哪些需要、期待或价值取向没有得到满足？我们把愿望说得越清楚，他人也就越可能作出积极的回应。例如，乙可以这样表达她的愿望：
p17.en: In this example, it is argued that the behaviour of others makes her unhappy; And B realized that her point of view made her unhappy. In Nonviolent Communication, we also encourage a better understanding of her aspirations: what her needs, expectations or value orientations have not been met? The clearer we speak of aspirations, the more likely others will be to respond positively. For example, B could express her wish in this way:

p18.original: “他们取消了合同，我很不高兴，因为我想重新聘用我们在去年解聘的员工。”
p18.en: “I'm not happy that they cancelled the contract because I wanted to rehir the employees we fired last year.

p19.original: 如果我们想利用他人的内疚，我们通常采取的办法是，把自己不愉快的感受归咎于对方。家长也许会和孩子说：“你成绩不好让爸爸妈妈伤透了心！”言下之意是，他们快乐或不快乐是孩子的行为造成的。看到父母的痛苦，孩子可能会感到内疚，并因此调整行为来迎合他们。遗憾的是，这种调整只是为了避免内疚，而非出自对学习的热爱。
p19.en: If we want to take advantage of the guilt of others, we usually do so by blaming each other for their unpleasant feelings. Parents may say to the kids, "You're not doing well to break Mom and Dad's heart!" The implication is that their happiness or their unhappiness is the result of the children's actions. Children may feel guilty when they see their parents' pain and adjust their behaviour to them. Unfortunately, this adjustment is made only to avoid guilt, not out of love for learning.

p20.original: 使用以下表达方式时，我们可能就已经忽视了感受与自身的关系。1）只提及相关的事情。
p20.en: When we use the following expression, we may already have overlooked the relationship between feeling and ourselves. 1) to refer only to relevant matters.

p21.original: “公司海报出现拼写错误使我很生气。”
p21.en: “I was angry with the spelling errors in the company posters.

p22.en: “This is a matter that makes me uncomfortable.

p23.en: 2) refers only to the behaviour of others.

p24.original: “我生日那天你没打电话，我很伤心。”
p24.en: "You didn't call on my birthday, and I'm sad.

p25.original: “你没有把饭吃完，妈妈很失望。”
p25.en: "You didn't finish your meal, Mom was disappointed.

p27.original: “我很伤心，因为你说你不爱我。”
p27.en: "I'm sad because you said you didn't love me.

p28.original: “我很生气，因为老板说话不算数。”
p28.en: "I'm angry because the boss doesn't count.

p29.original: 我们可以通过“我（感到）……因为我……”这种表达方式来认识感受与自身的关系。例如：
p29.en: We can understand the relationship between feeling and ourselves through the expression “I feel because I am”. For example:

p30.original: 1）“看到公司海报出现拼写错误，我很不高兴。因为我重视公司的形象。”
p30.en: 1) “I am not pleased to see a spelling error in the company poster. Because I value the company's image.

p31.original: 2）“你没把饭吃完，妈妈感到失望。因为妈妈希望你能健康成长。”
p31.en: 2) “You didn't finish your meal, Mama was disappointed. Because Mom wants you to grow up healthy.

p32.original: 3）“老板说话不算数，我很生气。因为我想有个长假去看弟弟。”
p32.en: 3) "The boss doesn't count. I'm angry. Because I want a long vacation to see my brother.

p33.original: 非暴力沟通需要：生命健康成长的要素
p33.en: Nonviolent Communication requires: elements of healthy growth of life

p34.original: 批评往往暗含着期待。对他人的批评实际上间接表达了我们尚未满足的需要。如果一个人说“你从不理解我”，他实际上是渴望得到理解。如果太太说“这个星期你每天都工作到很晚，你喜欢工作，不喜欢我”，那反映了她看重亲密关系。
p34.en: Criticism often implies expectations. Criticism of others is in fact an indirect expression of our unmet needs. If a man says, “You never understand me”, he really wants to understand. If the wife says, "You work late every day this week, you like work, you don't like me," it's a reflection of the fact that she values intimacy.

p35.original: 如果我们通过批评来提出主张，人们的反应常常是申辩或反击。反之，如果我们直接说出需要，其他人就较有可能作出积极的回应。
p35.en: If we make our claims through criticism, the response is often one of argument or counter-attack. Conversely, if we speak directly about needs, others are more likely to respond positively.

p36.original: 不幸的是，大多数人并不习惯从需要的角度来考虑问题。在不顺心时，我们倾向于考虑别人有什么错。例如，如果孩子把外套放到了沙发上，而没有挂在衣柜里，我们可能就会说他们是懒虫。如果同事没有听从我们的建议，我们也许会指责他们不负责任。
p36.en: Unfortunately, most people are not accustomed to considering issues from the perspective of need. In the event of discomfort, we tend to consider what is wrong with others. For example, if the children put their coats on the couch and did not hang them in the closet, we might say they were lazy. If our colleagues do not heed our advice, we may accuse them of being irresponsible.

p37.original: 有一次，我应邀调解南加州的一些农场主与工人的冲突。这些工人是外国移民，他们与农场主的矛盾越来越尖锐，争吵不断升级。会谈一开始，我就提出两个问题：“你们双方各有什么需要？为了满足这些需要，你们希望对方做什么？”一位农场工人喊道：“他们是种族主义者！”而一位农场主嚷道：“他们不尊重法律和秩序！”很明显，他们都在指责对方，而没有表达自己的需要。
p37.en: On one occasion, I was asked to mediate a conflict between some farmers and workers in Southern California. These workers are foreign migrants, and their conflict with the farmers is becoming more acute and their quarrels are escalating. At the beginning of the meeting, I asked two questions: “What are your needs? What do you expect each other to do to meet these needs? “They are racists!” says a farm worker. “They do not respect law and order.” “It is clear that they are accusing each other of not expressing their needs.

p38.original: 还有一次，为了增进信任，一些以色列人和一些巴勒斯坦人走到了一起。在会谈开始时，我问了同样的问题：“你们现在需要什么？为了满足这些需要，你们希望对方做什么？”然而，一位巴勒斯坦人接着就说道：“你们的所作所为和纳粹一样！”这当然很难得到以色列人友善的回应。
p38.en: On another occasion, in order to increase confidence, some Israelis and some Palestinians came together. At the beginning of the meeting, I asked the same question: “What do you need now? What do you expect each other to do to meet these needs? However, a Palestinian went on to say, “What you did was like the Nazis!” It is, of course, very difficult to get a friendly response from Israelis.

p39.original: 一位来自以色列的妇女立即站起来驳斥他：“胡说八道！”他们来这里本来是为了改善关系，可是，他们的对话只是使关系变得更糟。发生这样的情况，一般是因为双方都习惯于指责对方。在这个例子中，如果这位妇女想表达她的需要和请求，她也许会说：“我希望我们能互相尊重。你刚才评论我们的行为方式，我想请你谈谈，你的评论针对的是怎样的行为？”
p39.en: A woman from Israel immediately stood up and rejected him: “Bullshit! They came here to improve relations, but their dialogue only made them worse. This is usually the case because both sides are used to accusing each other. In this example, if the woman wanted to express her needs and requests, she might say, “I hope we can respect each other. I would like to ask you to comment on how we behave. What is your comment about?

p40.original: 根据我长期以来的经验，一旦人们开始谈论需要，而不指责对方，他们就有可能找到办法来满足双方的需要。以下是一些我们每个人都有的基本需要：
p40.en: In my long experience, once people begin to talk about needs without accusing each other, it is possible for them to find a way to meet the needs of both sides. The following are some of the basic needs of each of us:

p42.original: 选择梦想／目标／方向 Choosing dreams/goals/values

p43.original: 自由制定计划来实现这些梦想、目标和方向
p43.en: Free to plan for the realization of these dreams, goals and directions

p44.original: Choosing plans for fulfilling one's dreams， goals，values
p44.en: Choosing plans for fulfilling one's dreams， goals，values

p46.original: 庆祝生命的创造力以及梦想的实现
p46.en: Celebrating the creativity of life and the fulfilment of dreams.

p47.original: Celebrate the creation of life and dreams fulfilled
p47.en: Celebrate the creation of life and dreams fulfilled

p48.original: 纪念人生的失落：亲人的去世或梦想的破灭等（表达悲伤）
p48.en: Commemoration of the loss of life: the death of a loved one or the breakdown of a dream, etc. (expression of sorrow)

p49.original: Celebrate losses： loved ones， dreams， etc. mourning
p49.en: Celebrate losses： loved ones， dreams， etc. mourning

p51.original: 真诚Authenticity 创造Creativity 意义Meaning 自我肯定Self-worth
p51.en: True Autonomy Creates Creative Meaning Meaning Self-Assessment Self-Worth

p53.original: 空气Air 食物Food 运动 Movement， exercise

p54.original: 免于病毒、细菌、昆虫及肉食性动物的伤害
p54.en: Protection from viruses, bacteria, insects and predators

p55.original: Protection from life-threatening forms of life：
p55.en: Protection from life-threatening forms of life：

p57.original: 休息Rest 住所Shelter 触摸Touch 水Water

p61.original: 美Beauty 和谐Harmony 激励Inspiration 秩序Order 平静Peace
p61.en: American Beauty Harmony Incentives Inspiration Order Order Peace

p63.original: 接纳Acceptance 欣赏Apprecation 亲密关系Closeness 社区Community 体贴Consideration 成长Contribute to the enrichment of life
p63.en: Accepting Acceptance and enjoying the Apprectioning Communities Community Council to the establishment of life

p65.original: 诚实（诚实使我们能够认识和超越自己的局限性）
p65.en: Honesty (honesty enables us to recognize and transcend our limitations)

p66.original: Honesty（the empowering honesty that enables us to learn from our limitations）
p66.en: Honesty（the empowering honesty that enables us to learn from our limitations）

p67.original: 爱Love 信心Reassurance 尊重Respect 支持Support 信任Trust 理解Understanding非暴力沟通把需要看作是有助于生命健康成长的要素，而不是某种具体的行为。一种要素是否被当作需要，关键在于它能否促进生命的健康成长。
p67.en: Love Love Confidence Respect supports the Support Trust understanding that Understanding Nonviolent Communication sees need as a factor that helps a healthy growth of life, not as a specific act. Whether an element is treated as a need is crucial to its ability to promote the healthy growth of life.

p69.original: 社会文化并不鼓励我们表达个人需要。对于妇女来说，尤其如此。长期以来，妇女的形象和自我牺牲联系在一起。一旦把照顾他人当作最高职责，她们也就会倾向于忽视个人的需要。
p69.en: Socioculturalism does not encourage us to express our individual needs. This is particularly true for women. The image of women has long been linked to self-sacrifice. Once caring for others is considered the highest responsibility, they also tend to ignore the needs of individuals.

p70.original: 在一次研讨班中，我们就社会文化对妇女的影响展开了讨论。在社会文化的影响下，许多妇女在表达请求时感到别扭，好像做错了什么。例如，她可能不会说：“我今天累坏了，晚上想休息。”相反，她的话听起来也许就像是辩护词：“你知道我一整天都没歇过，我熨了所有的衬衣，把这周的脏衣服都洗了，准备了午餐和晚餐，还出去买了东西……你是否可以……？”“不！”她委婉的请求非但没有被接受，反而马上被拒绝了。她试图证明她应当获得某种权利。然而，对方的拒绝似乎再次表明她的需要微不足道。如果我们不看重自己的需要，别人可能也不会。实际上，如果直接说出需要，获得积极回应的可能性就会增加。
p70.en: In a workshop, we discussed the impact of socio-culturalism on women. Many women feel uncomfortable and seem to have done something wrong in expressing their requests, influenced by socio-cultural factors. For example, she might not say, “I'm exhausted today and I want to rest at night. On the contrary, her words may sound like a defense: "You know I haven't been resting all day, I ironed all my shirts, washed all week's dirty clothes, prepared lunch and dinner, and went out and bought something... "No! Instead of being accepted, her euphemism was immediately rejected. She tried to prove that she deserved some sort of right. However, the refusal of the other party appears to indicate once again that her needs are negligible. If we do not take our needs seriously, others may not. Indeed, the possibility of a positive response increases when the need is directly stated.

p71.original: 在另一次研讨班中，一些女士谈到对表达个人需要的畏惧。我母亲参加了那次研讨班。她突然站了起来，离开了房间，很久都没有回来。回来时，她脸色很苍白。我问道：“妈妈，你还好吗？”
p71.en: In another workshop, some women spoke of fear of expressing their individual needs. My mother attended that seminar. She suddenly stood up, left the room and hasn't come back for a long time. When she came back, she looked pale. I said, "Mom, are you okay?

p72.original: “还好，”她回答说，“刚才想起了一件事情，心里极为难受。”
p72.en: “Well,” she replied, “There was something that came to mind, and it was very painful.

p74.original: “36年来，我一直在生你父亲的气，我认为他不在乎我的感受。我终于意识到，我从没有和他说我想要什么。”
p74.en: “For 36 years, I've been mad at your father, and I don't think he cares about my feelings. I finally realized I never told him what I wanted.

p75.original: 是的。在我的记忆中，她总是委婉地表达自己，而不直接说她需要什么。
p75.en: Yeah. In my memory, she's always euphemisms, not just saying what she needs.

p76.original: 为什么会这样呢？她回忆说，小时候家里极为贫困，只要她想拥有一点东西，哥哥和姐姐就会教训她：“你知道家里很穷，怎么还这么贪心！你以为家里就你一个人？”于是，她也就不敢说她需要什么。
p76.en: Why is that? She recalls that when she was a child, she was extremely poor, and if she wanted to have something, he and her sister would teach her the lesson: "You know how greedy the family is! You think you're the only one at home? So she didn't dare say what she needed.

p77.original: 有一次，她妹妹在阑尾手术后得到了一个漂亮的小钱包。妈妈那时14岁。她是多么想要那样一个装饰有小珠子的钱包啊！但她不敢说。接下来发生什么呢？她假装病痛，并一直隐瞒家人。家里人带她去看了几个医生。医生无法作出诊断，于是就决定做手术检查。对妈妈来说，这太冒险了。不过，她最后如愿以偿，得到了一个一模一样的小钱包。收到礼物的喜悦让她暂时忘记了手术后身体的痛苦。接着，有两个护士走进了病房，其中一个把温度计放在她的嘴里。妈妈这时把钱包递给另一个护士看。护士很惊讶，说道：“哦。给我的？为什么？谢谢！”她收下了钱包！妈妈不知所措，她不知道该怎么告诉那位护士：“我不是这个意思，请把钱包还给我。”这个不幸的故事告诉我们，一个人如果无法说出自己的需要，会是多么的痛苦！
p77.en: One time, her sister got a pretty little wallet after the appendix surgery. Mom was 14. How she wanted to be a purse with little beads! But she didn't dare say. What happens next? She pretended to be sick and kept her family a secret. The family took her to see several doctors. The doctor was unable to make a diagnosis and decided to perform an surgical examination. It's too risky for Mom. However, she finally got what she wanted and got the same little wallet. The joy of receiving gifts has left her temporarily oblivious to post-operative physical pain. Two nurses then entered the ward, one of them putting the thermometer in her mouth. Mom's handing her wallet to another nurse at this time. The nurse was surprised and said, "Oh. For me? Why? Thank you! She took her wallet! Mother was overwhelmed and she didn't know how to tell the nurse: “I didn't mean it, please give me my wallet back. This unfortunate story tells us how painful it is if a person cannot say what he needs!

p78.original: 从“情感的奴隶”到“生活的主人”
p78.en: From "Slave of Emotion" to "The Master of Life"

p79.original: 对于大多数的人来说，个人成长一般会经历三个阶段。
p79.en: For the majority of the population, personal growth generally goes through three stages.

p81.original: 在这个阶段，我们相信自己需要为他人负责——让他人快乐是我们的义务。如果别人不高兴，我们就会感到不安，觉得自己有责任做点什么。此时，我们特别容易把亲人看作是负担。
p81.en: At this stage, we believe that we need to be responsible for others — it is our duty to make them happy. If others are unhappy, we feel uncomfortable and feel responsible for doing something. At this time, it is particularly easy for us to regard our loved ones as a burden.

p82.original: 显然，这会伤害到彼此的关系。我常听人这样谈论亲密关系：“我真的害怕与人亲近。每次看到伴侣处于痛苦之中，我就极为沮丧，感到窒息，甚至认为自己是一个囚犯。于是，我就想尽快摆脱这段关系。”许多人认为，爱情就是牺牲自己来满足爱人的需要。刚谈恋爱时，他们对恋人的关心是自发的。那时，彼此的相处是那么地惬意、融洽和美好。然而，随着关系变得“严肃”，他们开始认为自己有责任让情人过得开心。于是，爱情开始沉重起来。
p82.en: Obviously, it hurts each other. I've heard so much about intimate relationships: "I'm really afraid of being close. Every time I see my partner in pain, I feel so depressed, suffocated and even think of myself as a prisoner. So I wanted to get out of this relationship as soon as possible. Many believe that love is at the expense of itself to meet the needs of its loved ones. When they first fell in love, they took care of their lovers spontaneously. At that time, it was so nice, nice and nice to be with each other. However, as relationships become “serious”, they begin to feel responsible for making lovers happy. So, love starts to get heavy.

p83.original: 一旦面临这样的情形，我就会承认：“在恋爱中，我无法忍受丧失独立性。如果恋人过得很糟糕，我就会认为自己做得不够。我可能会由于不堪重负而提出分手。”然而，如果意识不到感受的根源在于自身，我可能就会指责恋人：“你太依赖我了，我能力有限，我们分手吧！”此时，如果我的朋友能够倾听我的痛苦，她也许会说：“你认为你必须照顾好我。这让你觉得自己失去了自由，是吗？”如果她反过来指责我：“我的要求过分了吗？”那么，我们的关系很可能就会陷入僵局，甚至难以为继。
p83.en: And when that happens, I admit: “In love, I can't stand losing my independence. If a lover had a bad life, I would have thought I was not doing enough. I might break up because I'm overburdened. However, if I don't realize that it's my own fault, I may blame my lover: “You're too dependent on me, I'm too limited, let's break up! At this point, if my friend could listen to my pain, she might say, “You think you have to take good care of me. It makes you feel free, doesn't it? "If she accuses me in turn, "Is my request too much? Then our relationship is likely to be deadlocked or even unsustainable.

p85.original: 在这个阶段，我们发现，为他人的情绪负责，牺牲自己迎合他人，代价实在很大。想到日子过得这么憋屈，我们可能会很恼怒。此时，如果遭遇他人的痛苦，我们可能就会无动于衷：“这是你自己的问题！和我有什么关系？！”虽然不再愿意为他人负责，但我们还心存疑虑。因此，我们的态度也就显得生硬。
p85.en: At this stage, we find it very costly to be responsible for the emotions of others and to sacrifice ourselves for others. We might be angry to think of the time we've had. At this point, we may be indifferent to the suffering of others: “This is your problem! What does it have to do with me? I don't know. “Although we are no longer willing to take responsibility for others, we are still skeptical. Our attitude thus appears to be rigid.

p86.original: 有一次，一位女士在研讨班的休息时间兴奋地说，她很高兴认识到自己也曾是“情感的奴隶”。研讨班重新开始后，我建议大家做一个活动。这位女士坚决地说：“我想做点别的。”我意识到，她在捍卫她选择的自由——即使她的选择会与其他人的需要相冲突。
p86.en: On one occasion, during her break at the seminar, a woman was excited to say that she was happy to realize that she was also a “slave of emotion”. When the seminar is restarted, I suggest that you do an event. And the lady said, "I want to do something else. “I realize that she is defending her freedom of choice — even if her choice is in conflict with the needs of others.

p87.original: 于是，我就问她：“你想做点别的，即使那会与我的需要相冲突？”她想了想，然后结结巴巴地说：“是……嗯……不是。”她的困惑反映了表达自己的需要只是个人成长的一个阶段。
p87.en: So I asked her, "Do you want to do something else, even if that would conflict with my needs? She thought about it, and she stammered and said, "Yes, um, no. Her confusion reflects the fact that expressing her needs is only a stage in personal growth.

p88.original: 这里，我想讲讲我女儿玛拉的经历。她以前是个“有礼貌的小女孩”，对别人的要求，总是百依百顺。她习惯于委屈自己来迎合他人。注意到这个情况后，我想鼓励她大胆地说出心里话。当我告诉她我的看法，她哭了。她很无奈地说：“但是，爸爸，我不想让任何人失望！”我回答说，真诚待人比委曲求全更为可贵。如果别人感到不安，我们可以认真地倾听，但无须责备自己。
p88.en: Here, I'd like to talk about my daughter Mara's experience. She used to be a “behaved little girl” and always asked for it. She's used to letting herself be nice to others. Having taken note of this, I would like to encourage her to speak boldly. When I told her what I thought, she cried. She said, "But, Dad, I don't want to disappoint anyone! “I replied that sincere hospitality is more valuable than mere pleas. If others are disturbed, we can listen carefully, but without blaming ourselves.

p89.original: 不久以后，我就发现玛拉有了变化。有一次，她学校的校长打电话给我。他告诉我，他在学校和玛拉说 “校内不能穿牛仔裤”，玛拉没好气地回答 “见鬼去吧，你”。我很高兴，玛拉终于能够说出心里话。当然，她还要学着尊重他人的需要——我相信，这只是时间问题。
p89.en: Soon, I found out that Mara had changed. One time, the headmaster of her school called me. He told me that he said at school and Mara, "No jeans in school," and Mara said, "Fuck you, you." I'm glad Mara finally said something. Of course, she also has to learn to respect the needs of others — and I believe it is only a matter of time.

p91.original: 在这个阶段，我们乐于互助。我们帮助他人，是出于爱，而不是出于恐惧、内疚或惭愧。那是自由而快乐的行为。此时，我们意识到，虽然我们对自己的意愿、感受和行动负有完全的责任，但无法为他人负责。我们还发现，人与人相互依存，损人无法真正利己。非暴力沟通正是想帮助我们既表达自己，又关心他人。
p91.en: At this stage, we are happy to help each other. We help others out of love, not out of fear, guilt or shame. It's a free and happy act. At this time, we realize that, while we are fully responsible for our will, our feelings and our actions, we cannot be held accountable to others. We have also found that people are interdependent and cannot truly profit themselves. Nonviolent Communication is about helping us express ourselves and care for others.

p93.original: 他人的言行也许和我们的感受有关，但并不是我们感受的起因。感受根源于我们自身的需要——非暴力沟通的第三个要素。听到不中听的话时，我们可以有四种选择：1）责备自己；2）指责他人；3）体会自己的感受和需要；4）体会他人的感受和需要。
p93.en: Their words and deeds may be related to our feelings, but they are not the cause of our feelings. The feeling is rooted in our own needs — the third element of Nonviolent Communication. When you hear something, we can have four options: 1) to blame ourselves; 2) accusing others; 3) to feel their feelings and needs; 4) Feel the feelings and needs of others.

p94.original: 对他人的指责、批评、评论以及分析反映了我们的需要和价值观。如果我们通过批评来提出主张，人们的反应常常是申辩或反击。反之，如果直接说出我们的需要，其他人就较有可能作出积极的回应。
p94.en: The accusations, criticisms, comments and analyses of others reflect our needs and values. If we make our claims through criticism, the response is often one of argument or counter-attack. On the contrary, if our needs are directly stated, others are more likely to respond positively.

p95.original: 社会文化并不鼓励我们揭示个人需要。对妇女来说，尤其如此。因为她们的形象常常和无私奉献联系在一起——这是社会对女性的期待。
p95.en: Socio-culturalism does not encourage us to reveal individual needs. This is particularly true for women. Because their image is often linked to selfless dedication — a social expectation of women.

p96.original: 对于大多数人来说，个人成长一般会经历三个阶段：（1）“情感的奴隶”——我们认为自己有义务使他人快乐；（2）“面目可憎”时期——此时，我们拒绝考虑他人的感受和需要；（3）“生活的主人”——我们意识到，虽然我们对自己的意愿、感受和行动负有完全的责任，但无法为他人负责。与此同时，我们还认识到，我们无法牺牲他人来满足自己的需要。
p96.en: For most people, personal growth generally takes three stages: (1) “slave of emotion” — we believe that we have an obligation to make others happy; (2) The “detestable” period - at which we refuse to consider the feelings and needs of others; (3) “The Master of Life” — We are aware that, while we are fully responsible for our will, our feelings and our actions, we cannot be held accountable for others. At the same time, we also recognize that we cannot afford to sacrifice others to meet our needs.

p98.original: “让私生子女像以前那样见不得人”
p98.en: "Let the illegitimate children be as invisible as they were before."

p99.original: 一位女士是救济食品发放中心的志愿者。有一天，她的同事在读报时气冲冲地说：“我们需要让私生子女像以前那样见不得人！”
p99.en: One of the women was a volunteer at the Relief Food Distribution Centre. One day, her colleague was angry at reading the newspaper and said, "We need to make our illegitimate children as invisible as they used to be!

p100.original: 在过去，听到不同意见，她一般只会在心里嘀咕对方的不是。这一次，她试着运用非暴力沟通进行交流。
p100.en: In the past, she had heard different opinions, and she had usually only been able to narrate in her heart what was not. This time, she tried to communicate with Nonviolent Communication.

p102.original: 女士：（首先试图了解同事的观察……）“你在读有关‘少女妈妈’的报道？”
p102.en: Ma'am: “At first, try to get a look from a colleague...”: “You're reading a story about `Girl Mothers'?

p103.original: 同事：“是的。真不可思议！有这么多少女未婚先孕！”
p103.en: Co-worker: Yes. It's incredible! There are so many teenage pregnancies!

p104.original: 女士：（接着了解她的感受和需要）“你担心她们的孩子没有良好的家庭环境？”
p104.en: Ma'am: “You're worried that their children have no good family environment?

p105.original: 同事：“当然！你知道吗？如果我那样做，我父亲会杀了我！”
p105.en: Co-worker: "Of course! You know what? If I do, my father will kill me!

p106.original: 女士：“哦，看起来在过去少女未婚先孕后果极为严重？”
p106.en: Ma'am: “Oh, it seems that the consequences of teenage pregnancy before marriage have been severe in the past?

p107.original: 同事：“是的！我们知道怀孕意味着什么！我们总是担惊受怕，而这些女孩却毫无顾忌。”
p107.en: Co-worker: Yes! We know what pregnancy means! We are always scared, and these girls are free.

p108.original: 女士：“你希望她们能有所顾忌？”
p108.en: Ma'am: Do you want them to have a problem?

p109.original: 同事：“至少恐惧和惩罚会起到一些作用！报道说有些女孩为了怀孕去和不同的男人睡觉！然后，她们生了孩子，由我们来买单！”
p109.en: Co-worker: “At least fear and punishment will do something!” Reports say that some girls sleep with different men for pregnancy! Then they had kids, and we'd pay for them!

p111.original: 此时，这位女士注意到两种不同的感受：1.对一些女孩故意怀孕感到震惊；2.对纳税人需要养育她们的孩子感到愤怒。她选择先关注第一种感受。
p111.en: At this point, the woman noted two different feelings: 1. Alarmed at the deliberate pregnancy of some girls; 2. Angry at the need for taxpayers to raise their children. She chose to focus first on the first feeling.

p113.original: 女士：“现在的人不顾名誉、后果和经济状况就未婚先孕，你很难接受这个事实？”（一般来说，在存在多种感受的情况下，一个人会诉说那些还没有得到倾听的感受。因此，倾听的人无须一开始就对各种感受同时作出反馈，而可以自然地从一种感受过渡到另一种。）
p113.en: Ma'am, “It is difficult for you to accept that people are pregnant before they marry without regard to honour, consequences or economic status. “As a general rule, in situations where there are multiple feelings, one can claim those feelings that have not yet been heard. Thus, listeners need not give feedback from the outset on the various feelings at the same time, but can naturally move from one to the other. I don't think so.

p114.original: 同事：“是的，你说最后是谁为这些孩子买单？”
p114.en: Co-worker: "Yes, who did you say paid for these children in the end?

p115.original: 女士：“你希望你纳的税能有更好的用途，是这样吗？”
p115.en: Ma'am: Do you want your taxes to be better served, is that so?

p116.original: 同事：“那当然！我儿子和儿媳想再要一个孩子。可是，培养孩子太花钱了，虽然他们都有工作，但还是做不到！”
p116.en: Co-worker: Of course! My son and daughter-in-law want another child. But it's too expensive to raise a child. They all have jobs, but they can't do it!

p117.original: 女士：“你想要一个孙子，是吗？”
p117.en: Ma'am: You want a grandson, don't you?

p118.original: 同事：“是的，但不只是我想要……”
p118.en: Co-worker: "Yes, but not just that I want to..."

p119.original: 女士：“……你还希望儿子能过上称心如意的生活……”（她继续倾听，让同事充分表达感受和愿望。）
p119.en: Ms. “...you also want your son to live a life of good will...” (She continues to listen and allow her colleagues to express their feelings and wishes in full. I don't think so.

p120.original: 同事：“是的。只有一个孩子是很可悲的。”
p120.en: Co-worker: Yes. Only one child is sad.

p122.original: 此时，这位女士感到同事已经平静了下来。她们沉默了片刻。她惊讶地发现，虽然她并不赞同同事的观点，但心中已无任何不满。接着，她通过非暴力沟通的四个要素表达她的看法。
p122.en: At this point, the lady felt that her colleague had calmed down. They were silent for a moment. She was surprised to find that, while she did not share the views of her colleagues, there was no dissatisfied. She then expressed her views through four elements of Nonviolent Communication.

p124.original: 女士：“听到你说‘我们应该让私生子女像以前那样见不得人’（观察），我有些担心（感受），因为我希望我们每个人都乐于助人（需要）。来这里领取食物的人，有些就是‘少女妈妈’（观察），我希望她们能喜欢这里（需要）。你是否愿意告诉我，小莉和她男友进来时，你是什么心情？（请求）”
p124.en: Ma'am: I'm worried because I want everyone to be happy to help. Some of the people who come here to get food are "mamas of young girls" (observation), and I hope they like it. Would you like to tell me how you felt when Lily and her boyfriend came in? (Request)”

p126.original: 她们又谈了一会儿。最后，这位女士确信，她的同事也很关心那些青少年，并热情提供服务。更为重要的是，她发现，她同时满足了自己诚实和互相尊重的需要。
p126.en: They talked for a while. In conclusion, the woman was sure that her colleagues were also concerned about the young people and were enthusiastic in their service. More importantly, she found that she simultaneously met her needs for honesty and mutual respect.

p127.original: 与此同时，她的同事也感到欣慰，因为她充分表达了对青少年未婚先孕的忧虑。通过不带敌意地分享彼此的观念，她们增进了理解，发展了友谊。如果没有运用非暴力沟通进行交流，她们的关系也许就会开始恶化。
p127.en: At the same time, her colleague was pleased that she had fully expressed her concern about teenage pregnancy. By sharing each other's ideas without hostility, they have improved understanding and developed friendship. If they do not use Nonviolent Communication to communicate, their relationship may begin to deteriorate.

p128.original: 练习三 需要和感受的关系

p129.original: 看一看，在以下例句中，发言者是否对自己的感受负责。
p129.en: See whether speakers are responsible for their own feelings in the following example.

p130.original: 1.“你将公司机密文件放在了会议室。太令我失望了。”
p130.en: “You have placed confidential company documents in the conference room. I'm so disappointed.

p131.original: 2.“你这么说，我很紧张。我需要尊重。”
p131.en: “I'm nervous when you say that. I need respect.

p133.original: 4.“你无法来吃晚饭，我很难过。我本来想和你好好聊一聊。”
p133.en: “I am sorry that you cannot come to dinner. I wanted to talk to you.

p134.original: 5.“我很伤心。因为你没有做你答应我的事情。”
p134.en: “I am sad. Because you didn't do what you promised me.

p135.original: 6.“我很沮丧。我希望我的工作已经取得更大的进展。”
p135.en: “I am frustrated. I hope that I have made more progress in my work.

p136.en: “Friends call me by my nickname, which upsets me.

p137.en: “You've got the prize, and I'm glad.

p139.original: 10.“你让我搭你的车回家，我很感激。因为我想比孩子们先到家。”
p139.en: “I am grateful to you for letting me ride home. Because I want to get home before the kids.

p140.original: 以下是我对练习3的看法：
p140.en: Here's what I think of practice three:

p141.original: 1.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。对我来说，这句话意味着他人的行为导致了发言者的感受。以下例句体现了发言者对自己的感受负责：“你将公司机密文件放在了会议室，我很失望。因为我希望重要文件能够得到妥善保管。”
p141.en: If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. For me, that phrase means that the behaviour of others leads to the feelings of speakers. The following example reflects the accountability of speakers for their feelings: “I am disappointed that you have placed confidential company documents in the conference room. Because I hope that important documents will be kept safe.

p142.original: 2.如果你选择这一句，我们意见一致。
p142.en: 2. If you choose this sentence, we agree.

p143.original: 3.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。以下例句体现了发言者对自己的感受负责：“你来晚了，我很郁闷。因为我希望我们能坐到前排去。”
p143.en: 3. If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. The following example reflects the responsibility of the speaker for his own feelings: “You are late, I am depressed. Because I want us to sit in the front row.

p144.original: 4.如果你选择这一句，我们意见一致。
p144.en: 4. If you choose this sentence, we agree.

p145.original: 5.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。以下例句体现了发言者对自己的感受负责：“你没有做你答应我的事情，我很失望。因为我希望我可以信任你。”
p145.en: 5. If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. The following example reflects the accountability of the speaker for his own feelings: “I am disappointed that you did not do what you promised me. Because I wish I could trust you.

p146.original: 6.如果你选择这一句，我们意见一致。
p146.en: 6. If you choose this sentence, we agree.

p147.original: 7.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。以下例句体现了发言者对自己的感受负责：“朋友叫我外号，我会感到难过，因为我想得到欣赏。”
p147.en: 7. If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. The following example reflects the accountability of the speaker for his feelings: “My friend calls me by my nickname, and I feel sad because I want to be appreciated.

p148.original: 8.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。以下例句体现了发言者对自己的感受负责：“你得奖了，我很高兴。因为我希望你能得到公司的赏识。”
p148.en: 8. If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. The following example reflects the accountability of the speaker for his own feelings: “You have received the award, and I am pleased. Because I want you to get the company's appreciation.

p149.original: 9.如果你选择这一句，我们意见不一致。以下例句体现了发言者对自己的感受负责：“你大声说话时，我有些烦。我需要安静的环境来学习。”
p149.en: If you choose this sentence, we are not in agreement. The following example reflects the accountability of the speaker for his own feelings: “I am a little annoyed when you speak out. I need a quiet environment to learn.

p150.original: 10.如果你选择这一句，我们意见一致。
p150.en: If you choose this sentence, we agree.
